newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, June 20 - CPO productiom rose 55,900 tonnes or 7.6 percent to 790,600 tonnes in May or some 10,000 tonnes higher than our estimate. The better performance reflected a stronger-than-expected increase of 9.2 percent or 49,400 tonnes in output in Peninsular Malaysia. Production in East Malaaysia rose a modest 3.3 percent to 201,400 tonnes.
For the first five months this year production totalled 3.292 million tonnes. This represents a robust growth of 10.6 percent or 315,000 tonnes over the same period last year.

Latest partial data for first-half June show the performance of major producers/millers ranged mostly from up 5 percent to down 5 percent. Overall for the month we tentatively estimate production to show a marginal decline of one percent to 783,000 tonnes or little changed from our earlier expectations.

Palm oil disappearance in May remained good and also better than our estimate. It rose 52,800 tonnes to 778,200 tonnes (inclusive of refining losses) and trailed CPO production by 12,400 tonnes. Exports of palm oil alone rose to 626,600 tonnes from 579,200 tonnes (revised) in April and 555,700 tonnes a year ago.

End-May stocks of palm oil thus posted a modest rise of 12,400 tonnes to 711,800 tonnes. As expected the increase was entirely accounted by CPO stocks which rose 32,500 tonnes to 384,600 tonnes. Peninsular Malaysia accounted for all the increase when its CPO stocks rose 43,600 tonnes to 275,200 tonnes.

Stocks of PK/PKO rose 5,400 tonnes to 139,000 tonnes, oil basis. This lower than estimated rise was due to better than expected offtake. Also, output of PK was up by a mere 2 percent or 4,400 tonnes on account of poor yield.
For this month we tentatively estimate palm oil stocks to rise 60,000 tonnes to 770,000 tonnes.
Palm oil exports are estimated at around 615,000 tonnes or somewhat lower than our estimate of 635,000 tonnes in May.

CPO futures price movements this week had been somewhat choppy. For some mysterious reasons, price fell 11-16 ringgit Monday afternoon following the release of PORLA figures which showed stocks some 30,000 tonnes lower than estimate and a modest 12,400 tonnes more than April.

Followthrough selling on Tuesday morning briefly forced the active September contract below the 1,160 ringgit support level. Strong commercial buying thereafter triggered a sustained recovery resulting in price chalking up gains of 28-33 ringgit in the last 3 days. Yesterday September settled near the high of 1,194 ringgit as the market's ability to hold on to the 1,180 ringgit level triggered active shortcovering activities in both futures and cash markets. Talk of Chinese buying interest in products also spurred buying. We expect today's closing to provide a better indication of next week's market direction. CBT soybean remained barely steady in lacklustre trading.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters)
